To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the presence of consumption habit does not alter the optimal tax policy in the pre-commitment case and (2) the government's ability to pre-commit to its future policy matters in the case where agents exhibit consumption habits.

(i) if the government can precommit to its future fiscal policies, the optimal marginal tax rates are the same as in the conventional model, (ii) if the government cannot commit, the high-skin type's marginal tax rates will be negative, whereas the low-skill types' marginal tax rates will not be affected.

the presence of consumption habit formation does not affect the optimal marginal income tax rate if the government can pre-commit, and that the optimal marginal income rate for the low-skill agent is ambiguous and the optimal marginal income for the high-skill agent becomes negative if the government cannot commit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the government's commitment power on the optimal marginal tax rates in the presence of consumption habit formation.
the effects of habit formation on optimal nonlinear taxation in a dynamic analytical framework.
the implications of habit formation for optimal nonlinear income tax policies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of consumption habit formation may lead to a lower marginal income tax rate for the high-skill agent, and a higher marginal income tax rate or a lower marginal income for the low-skill agent, depending on the government's commitment ability.
the presence of consumption habit formation may have an ambiguous impact on the optimal marginal tax rates.

the government's inability to commit to its future policy leads to a negative marginal tax rate for the high-skill agent and to a positive marginal tax rate for a low-skill agent, as compared with the conventional case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the government should be able to commit to its future policy if it is to achieve the standard optimal marginal income tax rate.
the government's inability to commit to its future policies is a necessary condition for habit formation to affect optimal marginal income tax schedules.
habit formation does not affect the government's ability to raise tax revenue in a dynamic setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of consumption habit formation may have a significant implication for the optimal design of the nonlinear income tax system, especially when the government cannot commit.
, in the presence of consumption habit, the optimal nonlinear income tax system may be time-consistent.
the government's commitment power is an important determinant of the effects of habit formation on optimal nonlinear income tax rates.
